title: Newcastle Office Furniture: Three Worked Workplace Briefs
metaTitle: Newcastle Office Furniture: 3 Worked Workplace Briefs | YOS
excerpt: Turn a six-desk office, growing team or boardroom refresh into a useful furniture brief. Compare example schedules, fitout responsibilities and quote checks.
metaDescription: Plan Newcastle office furniture with three illustrative briefs: a six-desk office, growing team and boardroom. Use schedules, scope checks and a free worksheet.
author: Your Office Space
heroImageAlt: Workplace furniture inspiration; the example briefs are illustrative
body:
A useful Newcastle office furniture quote starts with how the workplace needs to work: who attends, what they do, which items can stay and what the building allows. A list of desks alone leaves important decisions unanswered.

The three briefs below show how to turn those questions into a furniture schedule and a project conversation. **They are illustrative planning examples, not completed YOS projects, priced packages, measured floor plans or approved occupancy layouts.** The opening image is workplace furniture inspiration, not a photograph of these examples. Final quantities, dimensions, suitability, availability and services must be confirmed for your premises.

[Download the editable workplace-example brief (TXT)](/guides/newcastle-workplace-example-brief.txt). Copy the example that fits your situation, replace the assumptions and send it with your measured plan. No email is required to download it.

For help preparing your own scope, [discuss Newcastle office furniture with YOS](/furniture) or [send a furniture quote brief](/resources/furniture-quote#furniture-quote-form).

## Choose the decision you need to make

| Illustrative brief | Starting situation | Main decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Six-desk office | Eight people in the business, with an assumed busiest day of six working on site | Confirm whether six workpoints and a separate four-person meeting setting suit actual attendance and tasks |
| Growing team | Twelve workpoints required now, with a possible four more later | Test the future layout and compare one delivery with staged purchasing |
| Boardroom refresh | An existing room intended for eight participants | Test the table, chairs, storage and technology together before ordering |

These counts are assumptions for working through the method. They do not establish the area your business needs or how many people a particular room can accommodate. Start with a measured plan and assess the actual users, access and building requirements.

## Example 1: a six-desk Newcastle office

### The illustrative business brief

An eight-person business expects no more than six people to need a desk on its busiest planned office day. Staff use laptops and monitors, some visitors attend short meetings, and the business wants to keep two serviceable storage cupboards.

The first check is the attendance assumption. Record the busiest days, overlapping shifts, visitor use and any dedicated workpoint requirements. If seven or eight people regularly need desks at once, change the brief before shortlisting furniture.

### A starting furniture schedule

On a small screen, swipe the table sideways to read every column. Keyboard users can focus the table and use the arrow keys.

| Item | Illustrative quantity | Confirm before pricing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Workpoints | 6 | Top size, fixed or adjustable height, screens, equipment and included components |
| Task chairs | 6 | Suitable dimensions, adjustments and sample checks for the people using them |
| Mobile pedestals | 2 | Whether personal drawer storage is needed and whether it fits beside or beneath the selected desks |
| Existing cupboards | Retain 2 | Condition, dimensions, movement and compatibility with the measured plan |
| Small meeting table | 1 | Intended use, table supports, access and actual room dimensions |
| Meeting chairs | 4 | Chair movement and a separate arrangement for meetings involving the whole team |

Four meeting chairs do not provide a seated meeting place for all six on-site staff. Decide where a full-team meeting happens rather than discovering the gap after delivery.

Browse [individual desks](https://www.yourofficefurniture.com.au/collections/standalone-workstations), [height-adjustable desks](https://www.yourofficefurniture.com.au/collections/height-adjustable-desks), [task chairs](https://www.yourofficefurniture.com.au/collections/task-chairs) and the [mobile pedestal product options](https://www.yourofficefurniture.com.au/products/eternity-slimline-mobile-pedestal). Check the selected configuration and current product information; the schedule is not a bundled offer.

### The decision before ordering

Test desk use, storage doors, pulled-out chairs, visitor movement and the delivery route on the measured plan. Ask the relevant designer or adviser to assess suitability and access for the actual premises. Check proposed chair and desk adjustments together; Comcare's equipment-selection guidance considers tasks, equipment, adjustability and different users.

Separate the furniture order from electrical, data and any building changes. A desk with a cable tray does not automatically include installed power or IT setup.

**Make this example your brief:** [send your attendance assumptions, measured plan and retained items](/resources/furniture-quote#furniture-quote-form). If you are still comparing premises, use the [fitout readiness guide](/blog/office-fitout-readiness-newcastle) before committing to a layout.

## Example 2: a Newcastle team growing from twelve workpoints

### The illustrative business brief

A team needs twelve workpoints now and wants to understand the implications of adding four later. It also needs shared meetings and storage. Future growth is possible, but the business has not yet approved a date for the extra positions.

Treat future capacity as a design question first. A room that holds twelve desks today has not been shown to support sixteen simply because matching desks can be bought later. Test circulation, meeting demand, services and storage with the appropriate project team.

### Separate today's order from the future option

| Workstream | Illustrative current scope | Future item to assess |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Workpoints and task seating | 12 workpoints and 12 task chairs | An additional 4 complete workpoints, subject to a suitable layout and approved need |
| Shared meetings | 1 setting to be sized from meeting use and the measured room | Whether the larger team changes meeting-room demand |
| Storage | Inventory existing items before setting new quantities | Storage required for additional people, equipment or supplies |
| Electrical and data | Appointed providers assess the current equipment and positions | Capacity, cable routes and any work needed for the possible expansion |
| Delivery and installation | Price the agreed first stage with actual access details | A separately priced return visit, if purchasing is staged |

Compare [modular workstations](https://www.yourofficefurniture.com.au/collections/modular-workstations), [meeting-room furniture](https://www.yourofficefurniture.com.au/collections/meeting-rooms) and [storage](https://www.yourofficefurniture.com.au/collections/storage) against that brief.

### Compare the whole sequence

Ask for one proposal for the current requirement and a separate future option. If you are comparing buying now with buying in stages, record the supply price, storage implications, additional delivery visits, installation and any disruption separately. Confirm whether matching finishes or components can be supplied later; do not treat future availability or discounts as guaranteed.

For an occupied office, identify the areas that stay operational and who approves access, noisy work and IT changeovers. Use the [staying-open refurbishment guide](/blog/office-refurbishment-newcastle-stay-open) when building work or services alterations are involved.

**Bring the two stages into one conversation:** [request a furniture scope review](/resources/furniture-quote#furniture-quote-form). For the wider design and delivery workstream, [discuss client-side fitout project management](/contact?service=fitout#contact-enquiry).

## Example 3: an eight-person boardroom refresh

### The illustrative business brief

A business wants to refresh an existing meeting room for eight participants. It is considering a new table and chairs, retaining a screen and reviewing built-in storage. The retained technology and joinery have not yet been assessed for the proposed setting.

Eight chairs are a briefing assumption, not a statement that the room can accommodate them. Verify the room, door swing, chair movement, circulation, table supports and presentation sightlines before choosing a setting.

### A room-based schedule

| Item or interface | Illustrative starting point | Who needs to confirm it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Meeting table | 1 table; dimensions to be selected | Furniture team and the person responsible for the measured layout |
| Meeting chairs | 8 chairs; exact model to be assessed | Furniture team and workplace users |
| Existing screen | Retain if suitable | The client's IT or AV provider |
| Built-in storage | Review existing joinery; replacement scope unconfirmed | Appointed designer or joinery provider |
| Power and data | Locations and interfaces unconfirmed | Appropriately appointed providers |
| Delivery and assembly | Route, bookings and placement to be confirmed | Furniture supplier and the client's site contact |

Use the [boardroom furniture planning guide](/blog/boardroom-office-furniture-newcastle) for the room brief. Browse [meeting tables](https://www.yourofficefurniture.com.au/collections/meeting-general-purpose-tables) and [meeting-room chairs](https://www.yourofficefurniture.com.au/collections/meeting-room-chairs), then test a complete setting rather than selecting each item independently.

### A separate, genuine local project

The example above is fictional. A confirmed local YOS project is the **2025 Dynamic Business Technologies boardroom refurbishment at its Warners Bay headquarters**, where the approved YOS scope covered the table, chairs and joinery.

[Read the DBT case study and client feedback](/case-studies/dbt-boardroom-refresh). Its confirmed scope does not establish the quantities, costs, room capacity or outcomes of your proposed project, and it should not be presented as a complete construction fitout.

**Start with your actual room:** [send a boardroom furniture enquiry](/resources/furniture-quote#furniture-quote-form) with the plan, photographs, usual meetings and items you want to retain.

## When does a furniture brief become a wider fitout project?

A change to partitions, building services, joinery or the use of the premises may bring in additional design, landlord, approval and contractor workstreams. Ask the relevant advisers to establish those requirements for the site rather than assuming they are included in the furniture quote.

| Scope | Record separately |
| --- | --- |
| Furniture | Products, quantities, dimensions, finishes and inclusions |
| Delivery and assembly | Address, access, agreed delivery point, placement and packaging removal |
| Design and suitability | Verified measurements, user requirements, layout checks and decisions |
| Building and services | Appointed contractors, agreed works, dependencies and specialist checks |
| Client-side coordination | Brief, budget, decisions, programme and handover responsibilities under the agreed engagement |

YOS provides client-side project management, not building or head-contracting services. Appropriately appointed contractors perform building and trade work. Use our [Newcastle office fitout service](/office-fitout), [design brief guide](/blog/office-fitout-design-brief-newcastle) and [landlord-versus-tenant works checklist](/blog/landlord-tenant-fitout-works-newcastle) to prepare that separate scope.

## Build the budget from the schedule

Request an itemised quote for the exact models and configuration. Record product supply, delivery, assembly, optional installation, removal and specialist work as separate lines, with GST treatment and exclusions clear. Keep unpriced items visible as unconfirmed allowances, not zero-cost items.

A per-person or square-metre figure can help start a discussion, but it can conceal differences in shared rooms, furniture, mechanical work and other services. Use the [Newcastle fitout cost guide](/blog/commercial-fitout-cost-newcastle-2026) and [indicative fitout calculator](/resources/fitout-estimator), then develop the design and business-case budget together. The calculator does not replace a measured scope or supplier and contractor quotations.

For furniture-only comparisons, use the [installed-cost comparison guide](/blog/compare-office-furniture-quotes-installed-cost). The three briefs on this page intentionally have no fixed package price: different products, retained items, buildings and services change the total.

## Your Newcastle workplace brief checklist

1. Record the business objective and who approves the project.
2. Confirm peak on-site attendance, visitors, tasks and the target date.
3. Attach a measured plan, photographs and known information gaps.
4. List furniture to retain, relocate, replace or assess.
5. Separate quantities required now from any future options.
6. Identify power, data, AV, joinery and other provider interfaces.
7. Confirm the delivery route, building bookings and operating constraints.
8. Request comparable, itemised scopes with GST and exclusions clear.
9. Check suitability, exact inclusions and availability before committing.
10. Agree who receives, checks and accepts the completed furniture scope.

[Download and adapt the workplace-example brief (TXT)](/guides/newcastle-workplace-example-brief.txt), [explore Newcastle furniture planning](/furniture), or [send your project requirements](/resources/furniture-quote#furniture-quote-form). If construction or services form part of the project, [discuss the fitout coordination scope](/contact?service=fitout#contact-enquiry) separately.
